review: The hymn is the heart's petition: 1:1–8 is Ps 51:12 (לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא־לִי) with Ps 119:37 and Matt 5:16, 2:1–8 is 2 Cor 9:7 (כָּל־אִישׁ כַּאֲשֶׁר יָדְבֶּנּוּ לִבּוֹ) with Matt 10:42 (כּוֹס מַיִם) and 1 Pet 1:19, 3:1–8 is 1 Cor 13:4–7 with Eph 4:32, and 4:1–8 is Matt 11:29 with Gal 6:2.

The refrain אֱלֹהַי, תֵּן־לִי לֵב is identical in all four stanzas, as the printed يَا إِلٰهِي هَبْنِي قَلْبًا is; the Hebrew does not vary it, because each stanza then names a different colour of the one heart that is asked for.

1:2 דּוֹרֵשׁ אֶת־רְצוֹנְךָ — the Arabic يَقْصِدُ مَسَرَّتَكَ is 'seeking Your pleasure'; the Hebrew uses דָּרַשׁ, the verb of seeking God and His will (Ps 34:5, דָּרַשְׁתִּי אֶת־יְהוָה), rather than a general 'wanting', so the petition is for a heart oriented to God's will and not merely pleased by it.

2:6 לֹא תִּשְׁכַּח כּוֹס מָיִם — the Arabic لَسْتَ تَنْسَى كَأْسَ مَاء is Matt 10:42's cup of cold water; the Hebrew keeps the negative with לֹא and the concrete כּוֹס, because the line's comfort is that the smallest material gift is remembered, which an abstract 'reward' would lose.

2:8 לָנוּ נָתַן דָּמוֹ — the Arabic سَفَكَ عَنَّا الدِّمَاء is plural ('bloods'); biblical Hebrew uses דָּם in the singular for shed blood (Gen 9:6), so the Hebrew keeps the singular and the line still names the violent death rather than a medical quantity.
